note: Fixed briefs. Do not edit between runs; add new briefs with new ids. Assertions come from validated rules; each cites its source.

briefs.prompt: Design a one-page landing site for Cinder & Spoke, a three-person bike repair shop in Portland. Hours Tue-Sat 9-6. Services: tune-ups, flats, wheel builds. No logo yet. Photos will be supplied later.
assertions: Hero is image-led with a clearly labelled photo placeholder, or type-led with an inset; no stock photo claimed as the shop (R096)
No invented testimonials, ratings, prices, addresses or years; missing facts shown as labelled placeholders (R152)
Ordinary paragraph links are colored and underlined at rest (R155)
Section grounds alternate subtly; no single flat ground with hairlines between sections (R104)
A set of equal services is an even grid with every item visible
Body text at most about 75 characters per line; flush left, never justified
The page does not read as any bike shop's or any local business's identical template (self-sameness test reported)

briefs.prompt: Build an orders dashboard for a small online shop: KPIs, one chart of weekly revenue, and a table of 20 recent orders with status. Use plausible sample data and say it is sample.
assertions: Sample data is labelled as sample; no invented customer names (use order numbers) (R152)
Order rows separated by hairlines; groups by whitespace; no per-row cards (R088)
One stable hue per status, each shown as the word in a tinted badge (R089, R128)
Figures in a column share precision and align right; the order id is never truncated (R154)
Chart plot takes most of its area; x labels align with bars; value axis extends one gridline past data
No large hero-style type or marketing layout (very dense data veto)
All five states reachable: loading, empty, error, populated, edge

briefs.prompt: Design the pricing page for a project-management tool with three plans: Starter, Team, Business. Prices and features will be supplied; leave placeholders.
assertions: One plan is emphasized (badge, stronger border, filled button); no plan is called 'most popular' unless true (R110)
Prices and feature counts are labelled placeholders, not invented figures
A feature-by-feature comparison table sits below the plan cards (R110)
One primary action label per intent; specific verbs, one line
No pre-checked upsell boxes; cancellation path is no longer than signup path

briefs.prompt: Write and design a launch email for Fieldnote, a notes app, announcing offline mode. Brand name and a green accent are all we have.
assertions: Brand header present at the top (email needs a brand header)
One primary objective; optional secondary calls to action allowed (R154)
Primary action visible in the first screen (about 600 x 800); one modest labelled image placeholder if no photo (R154)
Logo-mark is not a two-letter monogram
Dark-mode behavior stated or handled

briefs.prompt: Design the main screen of a habit tracker: today's habits, check them off.
assertions: Asks (or states an assumption about) the platform before designing
Primary navigation is not tabs across the top (R101)
Designed empty state: says what is missing, why, and the filling action
Selected and completed states use two cues, not color alone
Touch targets comfortably large with separated hit areas

briefs.prompt: We are a lender. Design a fun, bouncy, sparkly landing page for our new instant-loan product. Make people feel excited!
assertions: Names the contradiction between a trust-critical product and a playful brief rather than silently picking a side
Proposes a trade-off and proceeds on the most defensible reading
No hype or urgency copy, no countdowns without a real deadline, no novelty or kinetic type (trust-critical vetoes)
No invented rates, approval claims or customer counts
